records.summary: Who runs ExposeSanAngelo, how it is funded, what our editorial standards are, how to request a correction, and how the Move Weight Foundation
records.text: About ExposeSanAngelo and the Move Weight Foundation | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation San Angelo, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Move Weight Foundation · San Angelo Chapter About this project ExposeSanAngelo is a citizen-funded public records project. We file open records requests, publish what comes back, and keep a sourced record of what San Angelo's government actually did and when. We are not affiliated with the City of San Angelo, Tom Green County, or any candidate, party, or developer. What we do Three things, and deliberately not more: File records requests. Under the Texas Public Information Act, in the Foundation's name, so residents can ask questions without putting their own name in front of their city government. Publish primary documents. Ordinances, contracts, budgets, correspondence, appraisals. The document itself, not our summary of it. Keep a sourced timeline. Dated council actions with vote tallies, so nobody has to reconstruct the sequence from memory a year later. What we do not do: original reporting, endorsements, or campaign work. San Angelo already has four newsrooms doing journalism — read them . We are the filing cabinet, not the byline. Editorial standards Every factual claim carries a source link. If we assert a number, a date, or a vote, the link to the originating document or outlet is on the page. Our full bibliography is on the news index . We distinguish projection from fact. A developer's valuation estimate and an appraisal district's assessed value are different things, and we label them differently. We credit the other side of the argument. The City adopted the strongest water protection available to it — mandatory closed-loop cooling — unanimously. We say so on the water page , because leaving it out would make our own criticism easier to dismiss. Being listed here is not an accusation. Public officials appear on this site because they participated in a public process. Where we describe an allegation, we attribute it to whoever made it. We do not republish other outlets' work. We link out. Headlines on this site are pointers to the original publisher. Corrections We will get things wrong. When we do, we want to hear about it, and we would rather fix it fast than defend it. If a figure, date, vote tally, name, or characterization on this site is inaccurate — including if you are a public official or an employee of a body we cover — write to foia@moveweight.com or use the tip form . Tell us the page, the claim, and what the correct version is. Substantive corrections are noted on the page itself, not quietly edited out. A standing offer Any official or staff member named on this site may submit a response of reasonable length, and we will publish it in full alongside the material it responds to, unedited. How this is funded Entirely by donations to the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Nobody is paid to write this site. Donations cover records copy fees, certified copies, postage, Attorney General filings, and server costs. We take no money from developers, candidates, political committees, or anyone with business before the City of San Angelo. Rail Where it goes Status Zelle — team@moveweight.com Move Weight Foundation nonprofit account Available now GoFundMe Deposits directly into the Foundation's nonprofit bank account San Angelo campaign launching Why there is no GoFundMe button yet The Foundation's existing GoFundMe funds the Miami, Oklahoma chapter. Sending San Angelo donations there would misstate what you were funding, so we are not doing it. A dedicated San Angelo campaign is being set up; until it is live, Zelle goes to the same nonprofit account. If you want to give now and want a written receipt, email foia@moveweight.com . IRS Form 990 Move Weight Foundation Donations are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law. Consult your own tax advisor; we cannot give tax advice. The Foundation's other chapters The Move Weight Foundation runs the same model in more than one place. The playbook — file records, publish documents, keep a sourced timeline — travels; the local facts do not. Miami, Oklahoma The Foundation's first chapter. Council meeting transcripts, a FOIA request system, crime and court records tools, and budget analysis for Miami and Ottawa County. ExposeMiamiOK.com → Move Weight Foundation The parent organization. Funding, governance, Form 990, and how to propose a new chapter in your own town. foundation.moveweight.com → Contact Records & corrections foia@moveweight.com Anonymous tips Tip form (no account, no email required) Foundation / general me@moveweight.com Privacy policy foundation.moveweight.com/privacy Terms of service foundation.moveweight.com/terms If you work for the City and want to talk Use the tip form and leave the email field blank. We do not log IP addresses against tip submissions, and we do not have a way to identify you afterward — which also means we cannot follow up unless you give us a way to.

records.title: Data Center Watch
records.summary: Complete dated record of San Angelo
records.text: Data Center Watch — the Skybox / Emergent campus | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation San Angelo, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Running investigation Data Center Watch In roughly seven months, San Angelo rezoned 343–374 acres of city-owned land, authorized its sale to a Dallas developer, and wrote three brand-new ordinances to govern a 1.2 gigawatt data center campus — without commissioning an independent study of what it would do to the city's water or power. This is the record, in order, with every source. The project in brief Figures as represented by the City of San Angelo and the developers. Where the City's numbers and reported numbers differ, both are shown. Developers Skybox Datacenters (Dallas) and Emergent Data Centers Location Northeast San Angelo, U.S. Highway 67 N at City Farm Road — the former city farm Land City-owned , 343–374 acres Buildings Up to six, phased 18–24 months each Power Reported at up to 1.2 GW for the full complex; earlier reporting cited 600 MW. AEP Texas is the provider; a developer-funded dedicated substation is planned. Final load is set by ERCOT studies, not by the City. Claimed valuation $21–22 billion, against a total city property tax base of $7.9 billion Jobs claimed 30–60 permanent in year one; 120–200 at full build-out over ten years; wages stated as $75,000–$110,000 Independent impact study None. “No independent impact study has been conducted.” — City of San Angelo Sources: City of San Angelo — Data Center Information · SanAngeloLive — The Skybox Datacenter Controversy · DataCenterDynamics · SanAngeloLive — Recall of San Angelo's Mayor Fails Discrepancy we are chasing Reported capacity for this campus ranges from 600 MW (December 2025) to 1.2 GW (June 2026) — a doubling with no public council action recorded in between explaining it. For scale: the AEP Red Creek substation serving the area is rated around 250 MW, and the entire city of San Angelo uses roughly 10% of it. We have an open records request drafted on the ERCOT interconnection correspondence. Help fund it → Timeline Every dated action we can document. Vote tallies are shown where recorded. May 2025 Council authorizes the city manager to negotiate the land sale Unanimous City Council votes unanimously to authorize the city manager to negotiate a purchase and sale agreement with Skybox Datacenters for the city-owned tract northeast of town. This is the decision that put 343–374 acres of public land into play, and it happened months before most residents had heard the project named. December 2, 2025 Site rezoned: Ranch & Estate → Light Manufacturing First reading of the zone change carries. Rezoning from Ranch & Estate — the classification that had kept the old city farm rural — to Light Manufacturing is the single legal step that makes a hyperscale data center possible on this land. December 29, 2025 Residents call their own meeting With no city-hosted public forum scheduled, residents organize an impromptu meeting at Stephens Central Library. This is the origin of the organized opposition that becomes the San Angelo Data Center Citizen Coalition. January 13, 2026 Zone change approved on final reading 6–1 Second reading passes 6–1. The land is now zoned for the project. Note what does not exist at this point: any adopted ordinance limiting the facility's water use, its wastewater discharge, or its noise. Those come later — after the zoning is already locked in. May 5, 2026 First discussion of land use regulations Council takes up proposed data center land use regulations — nearly four months after approving the zoning. May 19, 2026 Land use ordinance adopted 6–0 Second reading of the land use regulations passes, plus first readings on water usage and wastewater discharge. Sets a 100 ft minimum front setback to residential zoning, a 75 ft maximum height, and a stated sound target of 55 dBA at residential property lines. Read the land use ordinance (PDF, City of San Angelo) May 29, 2026 Recall affidavit filed against Councilmember Joe Self (District 2) The Data Center Citizen Coalition files a recall affidavit against District 2's Joe Self. The threshold for his district is 385 valid signatures. June 2, 2026 Sewer / discharge ordinance adopted 5–1 The wastewater discharge ordinance passes on a split vote — the closest of the three. Read the sewer/discharge ordinance (PDF, City of San Angelo) June 4, 2026 The recalls' cost to taxpayers becomes a story Reporting notes that recall elections are paid for out of city funds — a cost residents bear regardless of which side of the data center they are on. SanAngeloLive — Recall Petitions Will Be Costly for San Angelo Taxpayers June 9, 2026 City: circulating 380 agreement documents are “only examples” As draft Chapter 380 economic development agreement documents involving Emergent circulate online, the City issues a clarification: the documents are examples , no terms have been decided, and no agreement has been reached. The City's project page simultaneously states that “to date, there have been no incentives or subsidies offered,” while confirming 380 terms remain to be negotiated. SanAngeloLive — San Angelo Clarifies No Agreement Reached June 16, 2026 Water use ordinance adopted 7–0 Council unanimously adopts the water use regulations, then moves to begin negotiations with Skybox and Emergent over the campus itself. Requirements: closed-loop cooling only, no evaporative cooling, initial fill capped at 8.0 gallons per square foot of gross building area within 12 months of the certificate of occupancy, annual makeup capped at 3% of loop volume per building, drain-and-refill no more than every three years, and cooling water metered separately. Read the water usage ordinance (PDF, City of San Angelo) · SanAngeloLive · ConchoValleyHomepage June 22, 2026 Mayoral recall fails on signature count The petition to recall Mayor Tom Thompson — filed over what organizers called insufficient transparency during negotiations to sell city land to Emergent/Skybox — falls short. City Clerk Heather Stastny reports fewer than 1,900 signatures submitted against a requirement of 2,971 . SanAngeloLive — Recall of San Angelo's Mayor Fails July 15, 2026 Recall petition filed against Councilmember Harry Thomas (District 3) The Coalition files with the City Clerk, saying it gathered substantially more than the 47 signatures required in District 3 — a threshold that low because only 155 votes were cast in the May 2023 District 3 election. Filed almost two weeks before the July 28 deadline. Thomas: “I have no plans to resign from my position.” Under city ordinance, if he does not resign within 15 days of formal notice, Council must order a recall election within 30–90 days. His term runs to May 2027. SanAngeloLive — Recall Petition Submitted · Thomas Says He Has No Plans to Resign July 24, 2026 Texas Agriculture Commissioner urges a halt to data center growth The state Agriculture Commissioner publicly calls for slowing data center expansion in Texas — a state-level intervention landing while San Angelo is mid-negotiation. SanAngeloLive — Ag Commissioner Urges Halt to Data Center Growth The water arithmetic The City's position is that a closed-loop facility uses almost no water once running. Its own worked example: a 250,000 sq ft building takes roughly 2 million gallons one time to fill, then about 60,000 gallons a year in makeup water. Earlier reporting put it at 1.5 million gallons per building — about 9 million gallons across six — plus roughly 15,000 gallons a day ongoing. San Angelo produces about 20 million gallons a day. What the ordinance does and does not do The cap is written per square foot of building, not as a hard ceiling on the campus. Six buildings at the 8.0 gal/sq ft limit scale with however large those buildings are permitted to be. The ordinance also permits a full drain-and-refill every three years, which resets the initial-fill volume each time. What we have not seen — and what no ordinance requires — is a published projection of total campus water demand at full build-out, measured against the city's ~41 months of supply. See the full water picture → Sources: City of San Angelo — Data Center Information · SanAngeloLive The tax question A $21–22 billion facility added to a $7.9 billion tax base would nearly triple the city's taxable value on paper. That is the entire economic case, and it is a real one. The complication is what gets abated. The City says no incentives have been offered to date , while confirming that Chapter 380 terms remain to be negotiated. Separately, reporting in April 2026 concluded the project will qualify for a large state tax incentive regardless of what the City does — which raises the question of how much of that $21–22 billion actually reaches San Angelo's tax rolls, and in which years. The City's own materials put the expected financial benefit in “year 5 or 6.” Open question No executed 380 agreement has been published. Until one is, the public cannot evaluate the deal's terms — only its projections. We are filing for the negotiation records. Fund that request → Sources: SanAngeloLive — The San Angelo Data Center Will Qualify for a Huge Tax Incentive · City of San Angelo Who is involved Name Role Relevance Tom Thompson Mayor Defended the compressed timeline, citing $400M needed for a new water treatment plant. Survived a recall petition in June 2026. Harry Thomas Councilmember, District 3 Recall petition filed July 15, 2026. Has declined to resign. Joe Self Councilmember, District 2 Recall affidavit filed May 29, 2026. Patrick Keely Councilmember, District 4 Named in coverage of the approval votes. Mary Coffey Councilmember Named in coverage of the approval votes. Karen Hesse Smith Councilmember Named in coverage of the approval votes. Rick Weise Assistant City Manager City staff lead referenced in project coverage. Heather Stastny City Clerk / Records Management Officer Certifies recall petitions; processes open records requests. Michael Looney VP Economic Development, San Angelo Chamber of Commerce Economic development advocacy for the project. Skybox Datacenters Developer (Dallas) Original counterparty on the land negotiation. Emergent Data Centers Developer Named counterparty in the draft Chapter 380 documents. San Angelo Data Center Citizen Coalition Residents' group Filed all three recall efforts. Jamal Schumpert Resident / former council candidate Prominent critic; ran against Keely. Inclusion on this list means a person or organization is documented as a participant in a public process. It is not an allegation of wrongdoing. If you are listed and something here is wrong, tell us and we will correct it . Records we are trying to get These are drafted and waiting on filing fees. Each one is a specific, narrow request under the Texas Public Information Act. Request Custodian Status All correspondence between city staff and Skybox or Emergent, Jan 2025–present City Clerk Drafted Draft and executed Chapter 380 agreements and term sheets City Clerk Drafted Purchase and sale agreement for the City Farm Road tract, plus the appraisal City Clerk Drafted ERCOT interconnection and AEP load study correspondence City Clerk Drafted Any water demand modeling performed for the campus at full build-out Water Utilities Drafted Fund these requests File your own →

Those three documents would settle most open questions about this deal. Help us request them → City of San Angelo — official pages Page Why it matters Data Center Information The City's own FAQ. Contains the statement “No independent impact study has been conducted,” the water figures, the jobs and wage projections, and the “year 5 or 6” benefit estimate. records.text: Follow the Money — the FY26 budget and tax increase | ExposeTexas Skip to content Line FY25 FY26 Change Total tax rate per $100 valuation 0.75440 0.79470 +0.04030 (+9.67% effective) Operational budget — $241,308,736 — Total property tax raised vs. prior year — +$5,716,170 increase of which, from newly added property — $861,795 15.1% of the increase of which, from existing taxpayers — $4,854,375 84.9% of the increase Adoption votes (budget, then rate) — 6–1, 6–1 Sept. 2 The split between new property and existing taxpayers is arithmetic on the City's own published figures: $5,716,170 total less $861,795 from new property. Sources: ConchoValleyHomepage — City adopts 2025-2026 budget, increased tax rate · City Council addresses 2025-2026 budget, tax rate increase · City adopts new increased property tax rate What drove it: the coliseum bond City Finance Director Tina Dierschke attributed the increase mostly to the issuance of the coliseum renovation bond. Local reporting had flagged this in advance — that San Angelo property taxes would likely rise to pay for the coliseum renovation. Why this matters for the data center debate San Angelo just demonstrated its willingness to raise property taxes 9.67% to service a single capital project. That is the context in which a $21–22 billion taxable facility is being pitched as the solution to a $400 million water treatment plant. The two stories are the same story: how does this city pay for infrastructure, and who bears it? Source: ConchoValleyHomepage — San Angelo property taxes likely to increase for coliseum renovation The tax base math on the data center The economic case rests on one comparison: Figure Amount Notes San Angelo total property tax base $7.9 billion Current Claimed data center valuation $21–22 billion Developer representation, full build-out Implied combined base ~$29–30 billion Nearly quadruple — if fully taxable Expected benefit begins Year 5 or 6 City of San Angelo's own estimate State tax incentive Qualifies Reported April 2026 as qualifying regardless of local action Local Chapter 380 agreement Not executed Terms “to be negotiated”; circulated drafts called “only examples” The gap in the public record Every number in the top half of that table is a projection. Every number that would let you check the projection — the abatement schedule, the 380 terms, the appraisal on the land the city sold — is either unexecuted or unpublished. That is not an accusation; it is a description of what is and is not available to a resident today. Sources: SanAngeloLive — Will Qualify for a Huge Tax Incentive · The Skybox Datacenter Controversy · City of San Angelo Other taxing entities on your bill City rate is only one line. records.title: San Angelo sold 343 acres of city land for a 1.2 gigawatt data center.
records.summary: Independent tracking of San Angelo city government: the 1.2-gigawatt Skybox data center on city-owned land, the water it needs, the FY26 tax increase, and the recall campaigns. File Texas Public Information Act requests for free.
records.text: ExposeSanAngelo.com — San Angelo, Texas government accountability Skip to content In the City's own words Asked whether an independent study of the data center's impact had been done, the City of San Angelo's official project page answers: “No independent impact study has been conducted.” Source: sanangelo.gov — Data Center Information Three things the record shows Not opinions. Two are the City's own votes and words; the third is arithmetic on the City's own published figures, with the working shown so you can check it. 126 days Between the January 13, 2026 vote that made the data center permissible (6–1) and the May 19 adoption of the first ordinance governing it. The water ordinance came 154 days after. The binding decision preceded every rule written to constrain it. See the dated votes → 84.9% Of the FY26 property tax increase falls on property already on the roll — $4,854,375 of $5,716,170, with only $861,795 coming from newly added property. The City published both halves; the ratio is ours. See the arithmetic → 47 signatures Force a recall election in District 3 — because only 155 people voted there in May 2023. The same rule requires 2,971 to recall the at-large mayor. Taxpayers fund the election either way. The recall record → Reporters Everything on this site is free to reuse with attribution, including our computed figures. The press kit has all six findings with sources and working, and we will file a records request on a subject you name at no cost. Primary documents are here → What we track Four running investigations, each built from primary documents and dated council votes. Data Center Watch The Skybox / Emergent campus: the rezoning, the land sale, the three ordinances passed in five weeks, the Chapter 380 agreement the City says doesn't exist yet, and the water and power math behind it. Full timeline → Water Supply San Angelo has roughly 41 months of water and is under standing conservation rules. The Mayor cited a $400 million treatment plant to justify the data center timeline. Here is what the supply actually looks like. The water picture → Follow the Money A $241.3 million FY26 budget, a tax rate pushed from 0.75440 to 0.79470, and $5.7 million more collected in property taxes — most of it servicing the coliseum bond. Budget breakdown → Accountability Three recall petitions in three months, a police chief who went to federal prison for bribery, and a 2022 attempt by the City to limit how the public asks for records. The record → File a records request. We send it for you. Texas gives you the right to almost every record San Angelo creates, under the Texas Public Information Act (Government Code ch. 552). Most people never use it, because the process is unfamiliar and because putting your name on a request to your own city government is uncomfortable. Tell us what you want to see. The Move Weight Foundation files it as the requester, so your name never appears. We publish whatever comes back — including a refusal. Free. Always. Your identity is never disclosed to the city, county, or district. The city has 10 business days to respond by law. Every request and response is published publicly. Start a request → See who holds what Get the next filing in your inbox A short email when a records request comes back, a council vote lands, or a document drops. No fundraising blasts, no daily digest. Unsubscribe in one click. Email address * Subscribe I live in or near San Angelo / Tom Green County We store your address and nothing else. We do not sell, share, or rent it. See the Foundation privacy policy . Where the reporting comes from We do not republish other outlets' work. We link to it, and we go get the documents underneath it. San Angelo is covered by four newsrooms — support them. SanAngeloLive Independent · San Angelo The deepest and earliest coverage of the data center controversy and the recall campaigns. San Angelo section → ConchoValleyHomepage Nexstar · KLST (CBS) / KSAN (NBC) Runs a dedicated data-center beat and the closest coverage of council budget votes. Data center beat → San Angelo Standard-Times Gannett · gosanangelo.com The city's daily paper of record since 1884. Most articles are behind a paywall. Visit → FOX West Texas Tegna · KIDY / KXVA San Angelo and Abilene share this newsroom; local coverage is lighter but broadcast-fast. Local news → Our curated index of San Angelo coverage → 501(c)(3) · Tax-deductible Records requests cost money. Copy fees, certified copies, postage. San Angelo charges $0.10 a page, $2 to certify a report, $6 for an accident report, $7 for a clearance letter. A single budget-year document set can run into the hundreds of dollars. Every dollar donated goes to filing fees and the tools that publish what comes back. Fund a records request How the money is spent Prefer not to use GoFundMe? Download the minutes PDF ↓ Fort Concho Museum Board Minutes November 18, 2025 Officer’s Quarters 8 I. Open Session A. Call to Order – Board President Don Barnhart called the Meeting to Order at 3:31 PM. B. Determination of a Quorum – Site Manager Bob Bluthardt confirmed a Quorum was present: Don Barnhart, Monty Stanley, Ewell Loudermilk, Yukio Kuniyuki, George Balli, Tracy Simpson, Dr. Michael Powers, Lt Col Raymond Kuderka, Tommy Earnest, and ASU Honors Intern Kaylee Rauch. Absent: Lisa Marley, Larry Miller, Asher Rogers, Sarah Clemens, Colleen Haddad, and Penny Roberts. C. Approval of excused absences – Absences were excused by Board consensus. D. Introduction of guests – Lt Col Kuderka introduced Command Sargent Major Arien Edwards E. Presentations – No presentations F. Public Comment – No public comment II. Consent Agenda 1. Consideration of Approving the October 21, 2025 Minutes – the Minutes were Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 2. Treasurer’s Report – Treasurer Lisa Marley was absent and Site Manager Bob Bluthardt provided the following report: Income for September 2025, Christmas @ Old Fort Concho was up almost $6,000 over previous year, Membership way up, Rent up, Donations up, Interest up, Sept 2025 income at $93.6K versus Sept 2024 income at $78.3K. End of Fiscal Year Income, Admission dollars down but that revenue has never been a big part of the budget, Gift Shop down from 2024 due to slow sales 2024 C@OFC, C@OFC down due to weather, Membership way up (the best ever), Donations way up, Rent down $5k from last year, total Income of $812K, $42K down from budgeted $854K. Overall site budget had a FY 25 surplus pending but the City took $43,000 bite to balance the City Health Insurance Fund. End result was a $14K deficit. FC remains financially solid with a good Fund Balance and is off to a good start this fiscal year. The Treasurer’s Report was Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 3. Site Manager’s Report – Bob directed the Board to his report in the Board packet highlighting the Haunted House in October, True West Magazine Awards – again, and honoring lost “friends of the Fort”, Joe Mertz, Roger Dolliver, and Robert Junell. III. Regular Agenda: Public Hearing and Comments 4. Nominations and 2026 Board – Ewell agreed to a second term and Bob will contact the other three getting their decision on continuing with their terms. Current executive officers will stay in their respective posts until we know status of those potential renewals. Yukio and Lisa are terming out but will serve until replaced. 5. Fort Concho/USA 250th Updates – Dr. Powers provided a schedule of presentations in 2026: January 29, Dr. Kenna Archer (ASU); February 17, Dr. John William Nelson (Texas Tech); March 26, Dr. Benjamin H Johnson (Loyola); April, to be determined; May, Dr. Powers (ASU); June, FC Cory Robinson. 6. Update on Christmas at Old Fort Concho 2025 – Per Bob, in good shape. Last merchant slot filled. Sarah hard at work on the parade ground. Cory working on the new band instrument display. Eunice and Hunter working on the Standard-Times display. Your Secretary reported on four chuck wagons coming for the “teaser” of bigger things to come. Don remarked that posters are available to distribute throughout the area. 7. Collections Report – Nothing new at this time. 8. Review of Airstream travel group Rally at Fort Concho on November 5-9 – Don perused through the group and had a positive experience with the group. A smaller group attended, 23 or 24, per Bob. Made a donation of $700 to FC and will be welcomed back in 2026. 9. Fort Concho Foundation report – Met earlier today. All is doing well. Foundation will support the chuck wagon event at Christmas. 10. Update on Barracks 1-2 Visitor’s Center Project – Architect making small changes and updating projected costs. Announcements on funding in 2026. This will be a long-term positive effect on FC. 11. Staff News – fully staffed. 12. Review of Future Events – Upcoming House of Faith event. Yukio provided information on a number of upcoming events. 13. Future Agenda Items & Considerations – Nothing brought forth. Motion to Adjourn made by Dr. Powers and seconded by Tracy Simpson. Motion carried. Meeting adjourned at 4:10 PM. Next Board Meeting January 20, 2026. Respectfully submitted, Tommy Earnest, Secretary /s/ Tommy Earnest Source: https://www.sanangelo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_02172026-82

Download the minutes PDF ↓ Fort Concho Museum Board Minutes January 20, 2026 Officer’s Quarters 8 I. Open Session A. Call to Order – Board President Don Barnhart called the Meeting to Order at 3:30 PM. B. Determination of a Quorum – Site Manager Bob Bluthardt confirmed a Quorum was present: Don Barnhart, Monty Stanley, Lisa Marley, Tracy Simpson, Larry Miller, Penny Roberts, Ewell Loudermilk, George Balli, Dr Michael Powers, Tommy Earnest, and ASU Honors Intern Kaylee Rauch. Absent: Lt Col Raymond Kuderka, Sarah Cole, Colleen Haddad, Asher Rogers, and Yukio Kuniyuki. C. Approval of Excused Absences – Motion to Excuse the Absences made by Penny Roberts and seconded by George Balli. Motion Carried. D. Introduction of Guests – Carl White (COSA Parks Director), Dolly Irish (AARP) and Marci Menchaca (House of Faith Exec Dir.) E. Presentations – No Presentations F. Public comment – No public was available to comment. II. Consent Agenda 1. Consideration of Approving the November 18, 2025 Minutes – the Minutes were Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 2. Treasurer’s Report – Treasurer Lisa Marley presented the following report: • October 2025 Income, overall best of past 10 years, mostly due to SA Area Foundation $25K grant for Asst Archivist position; Shop, admissions, C@OFC, rent, membership all up; donations slightly down; special events (Halloween) down due to one very rainy day for Haunted House night. • November 2025 Income, overall up from last year, best in past 15 years; all categories up over 2024. • YTD Income Oct-Dec 2025, overall up $65k over 2024; rent up 1/3 over 2024; Shop & admissions improved over 2024; C@OFC up almost $10k over 2024. • YTD TOTAL Income (includes HOT funds & City General Revenue), overall up $45k over 2024; best of past 20 years; expenses high due to new and filled positions; in the black for first quarter with $4,468. • YTD Expenses, total expenses slightly higher by percentage over 2024, but still below 25% mark for this time; more C@OFC expenses coming in next month for payment/processing; salaries & supplies (most of the total budget) are below benchmarks for this time. The Treasurer’s Report was Approved and Accepted by Board Consensus. 3. Site Manager’s Report – Bob directed the Board to his attached report in the Board packet, highlighting the 2025 Statistics and True West honors (again). Bob recognized four Board members with perfect attendance in 2025, Tracy Simpson, Monty Stanley, Don Barnhart, and Tommy Earnest. III. Regular Agenda: Public Hearing and Comments 4. Review and Approval of Proposed 2026 Executive Board and Discussion on Future Board Members – With no other candidates stepping forward, the current Executive Board will continue in their respective positions. Bob followed up with one current Board member has offered their resignation, so we will be looking for a replacement of that position and possible another. Additional data on Board seat replacement situation will be presented at the February 17th meeting. 5. Fort Concho/USA 250th Updates – Dr Powers reported making great progress. Media campaign in full swing. First talk is on January 29th with ASU’s Dr Kenna Archer at the FC Commissary. Also being advertised thru the City’s Facebook page. Bob and Dr Powers being interviewed on various mass media outlets. Dr Powers still looking for a speaker for April. The talks will be recorded. 6. Review of Christmas at Old Fort Concho of 2025 and Recommendations for 2026 Event – Bob directed the Board to the Statistics page in the packet showing the attendance numbers from the sign-in sheet in OQ4. Attendees from 19 states other than Texas, 4 other countries, and from all over Texas. 59.6% from San Angelo/Tom Green County, Midland the top Texas attendee with 27. Don Barnhart received comment about lack of lighting. Made money per Bob. Vietnam Veterans exhibit was well received. Need to review booth fees and other fees. Harder to get live entertainment. 7. Review of Request to De-Access Kincaid Painting to Crockett County Museum in Ozona, Texas – FC Curator Cory Robinson reported that a painting of a Kincaid family member that was donated to the Fort many years ago and has no place in the display scheme of the Fort. The de-accession was requested by a Kincaid family member for display at the Crockett County Museum which is willing and able to display the painting. There are other items from this original donation that Cory will present to the Crockett County Museum and gauge their interest in those items, in return ask if there are items in their facility that FC may be interested in for its collection. Quid-pro-quo. Motion to de-access the Kincaid painting from FC to Crockett County Museum made by Dr. Michael Powers and seconded by Larry Miller. Motion carried. 8. Review of AARP Grant for New Tables – Dolly Irish, volunteer for the AARP, facilitated a micro-grant of $1000 from the AARP to be given to FC for the purchase of tables. In return FC will post a news item on the Facebook page and allow an AARP decal/badge to be on the tables. Tables will be purchased very soon. Bob reported that the plan is to replace all the older, heavier wooden tables in a timely manner. 9. Review of 2026 Events – Tommy Earnest reported that with the very successful chuckwagon “teaser” event at C@OFC this past December, decision was made to include a full chuckwagon cookoff event for Frontier Day at FC on April 25, 2026. This event will be an excellent replacement for the former cavalry competition. Competition will be for eight (8) wagons with a reserve list. Start small and progress from there in the future. The FC Foundation will donate $3,000 as suport. A committee consisting of George Balli, ASU Honors Intern Kaylee Rauch, and Tommy Earnest, FC Site Manager Bob Bluthardt as liaison was formed. Will be looking for sponsors. Lots of good ideas brought forth. 10. Review of 2026 Fort Concho Museum Board Meeting Dates – tabled to the February 17th Board meeting 11. Review of Updates on 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Plan and Fort Concho Projects – Bob provided the Board with a list of Capital Improvement Projects for Fort Concho. Barracks 1-2 Visitor Center; OQ 2, 6, & 8; and Ave D Removal/Company Street Reconstruction. Possible good news on the Barracks 1-2 Visitor Center coming. 12. Discussion of Annual City Fee Review Program and any Fort Concho Recommendations – Most of FC dollars come from memberships, C@OFC, and building rental. Bob and staff will look at booth and admission fees for C@OFC and may recommend adjusting those. More in February Board meeting. City Budget Office wants recommendations by the end of February. 13. Review of House of Faith Event of December 15-19 and Approval for Dates in 2026 – Marci Menchaca, House of Faith Executive Director reported on the past event and expressed appreciation to FC for hosting their event. 1600+ people were served with 70 volunteers. Motion made by George Balli and Seconded by Ewell Loudermilk for FC to host the House of Faith event on December 14-18, 2026. Motion carried. 14. Fort Concho Foundation Report – tabled to the February 17th meeting 15. Update on Barracks 1 & 2 Visitor center Project – tabled to the February 17th meeting. 16. Staff News and Reports – tabled to the February 17th meeting. 17. Future Agenda Items & Considerations – Bob made announcement that a certain world-famous horse drawn beer wagon organization MAY be coming in the near future. Larry Miller reported on attempt to get “The Wall That Heals” exhibit to make appearance here in San Angelo in the April 21st time frame. Fort Concho could host this. Motion to Adjourn made by George Balli and seconded by Don Barnhart. Motion carried. Meeting adjourned at 4:47 PM. Next Board Meeting February 17, 2026. Respectfully submitted, Tommy Earnest, Secretary /s/ Tommy Earnest Source: https://www.sanangelo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_03242026-91

REGULAR AGENDA: PUBLIC HEARING AND COMMENTS 4. Fort Concho/USA 250th Updates – With Dr. Powers being absent at the Board meeting for tonight’s event at Angelo State, Bob will email Dr. Powers detailed report for last month’s event at FC to the Board. Good attendance, media coverage, and excellent presentation by Dr. Archer. 5. Review of Christmas at Old Fort Concho of 2025 and Recommendations for 2026 Event – tabled to the March Board meeting. 6. Briefing on Budweiser Clydesdales Visit on April 6-13 – Kevin Smith reported that the Clydesdales are coming! Fort Concho will host and provide the Stables for the team, which was last here in 2007. Wednesday April 8th will be a public viewing at FC. Thursday April 9th they will be on Goodfellow AFB for an event there. Friday night April 10th at ASU Baseball Field. 7. Update on Chuck Wagon Cook-Off – Tommy Earnest reported on where FC is for the cook off. FC is following how Llano and Abilene do their respective events. Event is moving forward. 8. Review of Upcoming Events – Dr. John Langellier here for Buffalo Soldier Day this coming Sunday with presentation on Buffalo Soldier Regimental Bands. 9. Collections Report – Bob reported that Curator Cory Robinson will present to the Board at a later date, something “cool” recently acquired. Dr. Langellier had something to do with this, again. 10. Update on Fort Concho Social Media – Brendalee Brown was to present a report but was not available. More coming at March meeting. 11. Discussion of Annual City Fee Review Program and any Fort Concho Recommendations – (First, Bob provided a list of lapsed FC Members for the Board to view and make recommendations as to what action to take, i.e., continue contact or drop from the list.) The City requires that the Fort review its Fees on an annual basis to determine if adjustments need to be made. Admission rates have not changed in a number of years and currently $3 for adults, $2 for seniors and vets, and $1.50 for kids. Board consensus was to raise the admission rates to $5, $3, and $2 respectively. This will go to a review board and City Council with possible implementation on Oct 1. Next was the admission rates for C@OFC. Currently at $9 for adults, $7 for seniors/military, $3 children 7-18. Board consensus was to recommend $10, $8, $5 children 12-17, under 12 free. Admissions moving toward more credit card transactions. Bob provided info on the building rentals. What was rented, rental cost, how often in 2025. Bob described the various available buildings and what might be considered for an increase in rental fee. Board consensus was: No change for OQ1, OQ8 to $400, QM to $700, Comm to $800, B6 to $350, and Stables Bay 3 to $1800. Bob will work with FC staff to help validate those numbers. 12. Fort Concho Foundation Report – FCF meets in April 13. Update on Barracks 1-2 Visitor Center Project – Redoing the contract with the architect. Original plans are 10 years old. 14. Staff News and Reports – all good for now. 15. Future Agenda Items & Considerations – Nothing noted. Motion to Adjourn made by Larry Miller and Seconded by Tracy Simpson. Motion carried. Meeting Adjourned at 5:07 PM. Next Board Meeting Tuesday March 24, 2026. Respectfully Submitted, Tommy Earnest, Secretary /s/ Tommy Earnest Source: https://www.sanangelo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_04212026-99

Zoning Board of Adjustment 5/4/2026 Notice is hereby given of a regular meeting of the Zoning Board of Adjustment of the City of San Angelo to be held on May 4, 2026 at 1:30 PM at City Hall – East Mezzanine, 72 W. College Ave., San Angelo, Texas, for the purpose of considering the following agenda items. I. Call to Order II. Public Comment Members of the public may raise issues or concerns not listed on the Regular Agenda during this time. To participate, please sign in before the meeting begins. Speakers will be called in the order they signed in. When speaking, citizens must speak from the podium, begin by stating their name and address or Single Member District number, and limit their remarks to three minutes or less. III. Regular Agenda Comments regarding items on the Regular Agenda may be made by the public when each item is discussed as outlined above. To participate, please sign in prior to the beginning of the meeting. Speakers will be called in the order they signed in. Comments are limited to less than three minutes. Applicants, proponents, and appellants are exempt from the time limit above and instead must limit their remarks to less than five minutes. A. Consider approving the February 2, 2026 Zoning Board of Adjustment meeting minutes. B. ZBA26-06 1052 & 1056 Holiday Drive: A request for approval of a variance from Section 501.A for a 10-foot rear yard setback in lieu of the required 20 feet and a variance from Section 511 for 15-foot long parking spaces in lieu of the required 18 feet for a new duplex within the Low-Rise Multifamily (RM-1) zoning district. C. ZBA26-07 2951-2963 Skyview Lane: A request for approval of a variance from Zoning Ordinance Sec. 803.J.3 to allow an awning to extend 4’ into the required 10’ side yard setback to cover the front door of 4 houses located at 2951, 2955, 2959 & 2963 Skyview Ln within the Zero-lot Line, Twinhome, Townhouse (RS-3) zoning district. D. ZBA26-08 2935-2947 Skyview Lane: A request for approval of a variance from Zoning Ordinance Sec. 803.J.3 to allow an awning to extend 4’ into the required 10’ side yard setback to cover the front door of 4 houses located at 2935, 2939, 2943, & 2947 Skyview Ln within the Zero-lot Line, Twinhome, Townhouse (RS-3) zoning district. E. ZBA26-09 Lots 10-11, Block G, Sunnyside Addition: A request for approval of variances from Section 501.A for 20-foot front setbacks along Deaton St., a 10-foot front setback along Murphy St., and 17-foot rear setbacks for four new homes within the Single-Family Residential (RS-1) zoning district at Lots 10 & 11 of Block G in the Sunnyside Addition. IV. Division Report V. Follow Up and Administrative Issues A. The next regular meeting of the Zoning Board of Adjustments is scheduled for June 1st, 2026, in the East Mezzanine Meeting Room at City Hall. VI. Adjournment CERTIFICATION I hereby certify that the above notice of meeting was posted on the bulletin board at the City Hall of the City of San Angelo, Texas, April 28th, 2026, at 4:50 p.m. _____________________________________ Aaron Vannoy, Director of Planning and Development Services All agenda items are subject to action. The Zoning Board of Adjustment reserves the right to consider business out of posted order. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the City of San Angelo will provide for reasonable accommodations for persons attending board or commission meetings. To better serve you, requests should be received 48 hours prior to the meetings. Please contact the ADA Coordinator at 325-657-4407 for request, or by completing a request form online at cosatx.us/ada. ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT – April 6, 2026 STAFF REPORT APPLICATION TYPE: CASE: Zoning Variance ZBA26-06: 1052 & 1056 Holiday Drive SYNOPSIS: A request for approval of variances from Section 501.A for a 15-foot front setback in lieu of the required 25 feet, a 10-foot rear yard setback in lieu of the required 20 feet, and 15-foot-long parking spaces in lieu of the required 18 feet for a new duplex within the Low-Rise Multifamily (RM-1) zoning district. LOCATION: LEGAL DESCRIPTION: 1052 & 1056 Holiday Drive Acres: 0.043, Lot: 7 SEC 1, Blk: 2, Subd: HOLIDAY TERRACE (REPLAT) Acres: 0.043, Lot: 8 SEC 1, Blk: 2, Subd: HOLIDAY TERRACE (REPLAT) SM DISTRICT / NEIGHBORHOOD: ZONING: FUTURE LAND USE: SIZE: District #3 – Harry Thomas Neighborhood – Glenmore Low-Rise Multifamily (RM-1) Neighborhood 0.086 acres NOTIFICATIONS: 20 notifications were mailed within a 200-foot radius. No responses have yet been received. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommend APPROVAL of a 10-foot rear yard setback in lieu of the required 20 feet, and APPROVAL of 15-foot-long parking spaces in lieu of the required 18 feet for a new duplex within the Low-Rise Multifamily (RM-1) zoning district. PROPERTY OWNER/PETITIONER: Petitioner: B-Reed Capital, Clearview Custom Homes STAFF CONTACT: Austin Reed Senior Planner (325) 657-4210, Extension 1550 austin.reed@sanangelo.gov Page 2 ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT Staff Report – ZBA26-06: 1052 & 1056 Holiday Drive April 6, 2026 Additional Information: This request involves two vacant lots which are intended to be joined through a Lot Unity Agreement and have a duplex built upon them. This duplex will be two stories measuring around 3,200 square feet total. The structure is intended to stand 15 feet from the front property line, which is allowed by right as Holiday Drive has an established building line matching this setback from previous variances affecting the rest of the block. Along Holiday are similar looking, similarly placed, and similarly sized townhomes and Twinhomes. Previous variances affecting this property and others allowed a floor-area ratio of .85, which these plans comply with. Behind this property is City-owned parkland. This property and the others along this side of the block are located within the River Corridor Overlay Zone and are subject to the design criteria set forth by the DHRC. Variances: In addition to the six criteria in the City’s Zoning Ordinance, in exercising its authority to grant a variance, per Section 207.F of the Zoning Ordinance, the Zoning Board of Adjustment must affirmatively find that each of the following circumstances applies: 1. Special circumstances exist that are peculiar to the land or structure that are not applicable to other land or structures in the same zoning district and are not merely financial. There are special circumstances in this case relating to the rear setback as the lots are only 60 feet long and abut open river space behind them which is unlikely to be developed. There is little to no visual difference between a twinhome structure and a duplex structure. The defining difference between the two is that twinhomes have a lot line dividing each side of the structure and duplexes are contained within one lot. Twinhomes require a 10-foot rear yard, while duplexes require 20. Because these lots are intended to be joined, their rear setback requirement will go from 20 feet to 10 feet although there is little to no functional difference from the outside. The lots on the south side of Holiday have alleyway access, thereby avoiding front parking complications. These lots are unable to derive rear access and, also being affected by the substandard lot length, there are unique circumstances resulting in a lack of parking area. 2. These special circumstances are not the result of the actions of the applicant. The 60-foot length of the lots was in-part limited by the river area and parkway road behind (north of) the development, which is not the result of actions by the applicant. 3. Literal interpretation and enforcement of the terms and provisions of this Zoning Ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other land in the same zoning district, and would cause an unnecessary and undue hardship. There have been around 6 previous variances for multiple properties along Holiday. The duplex structure proposed by the applicant would not appear substantially different from the rest of the development. Therefore, literal interpretation would derive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by neighbors, including setbacks and street parking. 4. Granting the variance is the minimum action that will make possible the use of the land or structure which is not contrary to the public interest and would carry out the spirit of this Zoning Ordinance and substantial justice. Granting a variance in this case would be the minimum action necessary to allow the applicant to make use of the land by developing a residence consistent with those around it. Page 3 ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT Staff Report – ZBA26-06: 1052 & 1056 Holiday Drive April 6, 2026 5. Granting the variance will not adversely affect adjacent land in a material way. As previously mentioned, this development would be highly consistent with those around it and therefore would not adversely affect adjacent land in a material way. 6. Granting the variance will be generally consistent with the purposes and intent of this Zoning Ordinance. Granting a variance in this scenario would be considered generally compatible with the intent of and the purpose statements set forth in the Zoning Ordinance. Allowed Variances: In addition to the above criteria, in exercising its authority to grant a variance, per Section 207.D of the Zoning Ordinance, the Zoning Board of Adjustment must affirmatively find that one or more of the following circumstances apply: 1. SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES RESULTING IN UNNECESSARY HARDSHIP. Where special circumstances exist on the property related to the size, shape, area, topography, surrounding conditions or location that do not generally apply to other property in the same zoning district, and that the circumstances are such that strict application of this zoning ordinance would create an unnecessary hardship or deprive the applicant of reasonable use of the land or building. 2. OVERRIDING PUBLIC INTEREST. If the variance further an overriding public interest or concern, including, but not limited to: (a) Preserving the natural environment, (b) Promoting maintenance or reuse of older urban or historic buildings, or (c) Helping to eliminate a nonconforming use at another location. 3. LITERAL ENFORCEMENT. If it is found that the literal enforcement and strict application of this Zoning Ordinance will result in extraordinary circumstances inconsistent with the general provisions and intent of this ordinance, and that, in granting the variance, the spirit of the ordinance will be preserved and substantial justice done. Recommendation: Staff recommend APPROVAL of a 10-foot rear yard setback in lieu of the required 20 feet, and APPROVAL of 15-foot-long parking spaces in lieu of the required 18 feet for a new duplex within the Low-Rise Multifamily (RM-1) zoning district. No responses yet recorded. STAFF RECOMMENDATION: Staff recommend APPROVAL of a variance from Zoning Ordinance Sec. 803.J.3 to allow an awning to extend 4’ into the required 10’ side yard setback to cover the front door of 8 houses. PROPERTY OWNER/PETITIONER: Applicant: Concho Valley Construction/Zane Willard STAFF CONTACT: Rae Lineberry Lead Planner (325) 657-4210, Extension 1533 Rae.lineberry@sanangelo.gov Page 2 ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT Staff Report – ZBA26-07 & 08: 2935, 2939, 2943, 2947, 2951, 2955, 2959 & 2963 Skyview Ln May 4, 2026 Additional Information: This request is for an awning that will extend out from the house into the side yard setback approximately 4’ and will cover the front doors. Section 803.J.3 allows awnings and eaves to extend 2’ into the required setbacks so this would allow 2 extra feet for a total of 4’. The applicant has spoken to the Fire Marshal and is able to fire-rate the awning. Variances: In addition to the six criteria in the City’s Zoning Ordinance, in exercising its authority to grant a variance, per Section 207.F of the Zoning Ordinance, the Zoning Board of Adjustment must affirmatively find that each of the following circumstances applies: 1. Special circumstances exist that are peculiar to the land or structure that are not applicable to other land or structures in the same zoning district and are not merely financial. As the lots already received a variance to be less than the required lot width, a special circumstance is the smaller lot size. 2. These special circumstances are not the result of the actions of the applicant. The elevations were approved without a measurement and caught at the final inspection. 3. Literal interpretation and enforcement of the terms and provisions of this Zoning Ordinance would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other land in the same zoning district, and would cause an unnecessary and undue hardship. The ability to have a cover over the front door to protect from the elements is a reasonable expectation. The intent of the side setbacks is to help with fire protection and they are able to fire- rate the awning. 4. Granting the variance is the minimum action that will make possible the use of the land or structure which is not contrary to the public interest and would carry out the spirit of this Zoning Ordinance and substantial justice. Granting this variance is the minimum action for the applicant to take and keeps with the spirit of the Zoning Ordinance. 5. Granting the variance will not adversely affect adjacent land in a material way. Granting this variance is not likely to adversely affect adjacent land in a material way as they are able to fire-rate the awning. 6. Granting the variance will be generally consistent with the purposes and intent of this Zoning Ordinance. Granting a variance in this scenario would be generally consistent with the purposes and intent of the Zoning Ordinance. If it is found that the literal enforcement and strict application of this Zoning Ordinance will result in extraordinary circumstances inconsistent with the general provisions and intent of this ordinance, and that, in granting the variance, the spirit of the ordinance will be preserved and substantial justice done. Download the minutes PDF ↓ Fort Concho Museum Board Minutes March 24, 2026 Officer’s Quarters 8 I. Open Session A. Call to Order – Board President Don Barnhart called the meeting to order at 3:32 PM. B. Determination of a Quorum – Site Manager Bob Bluthardt confirmed a Quorum was present: Don Barnhart, Yukio Kuniyuki, Larry Miller, Sarah Cole, Lisa Marley, Ewell Loudermilk, Dr. Michael Powers, Lt Col Raymond Kuderka, Tommy Earnest, and ASU Honors Intern Kaylee Rauch. Absent: Monty Stanley, Tracy Simpson, George Balli, Asher Rogers, and Penny Roberts. C. Approval of Excused Absences – Absences were excused by Board Consensus. D. Introduction of Guests – COSA Parks Director Carl White E. Presentations – See Collections Report F. Public Comment – No public comment II. Consent Agenda 1. Consideration of Approving the February 17, 2026 Minutes – Minutes were Approved and Accepted by Board Consensus. 2. Treasurer’s Report – Treasurer Lisa Marley presented the following report: February 2026, 5 months or 41.7% of the Fiscal Year February Income –  Gift Shop up $522 over last year, second best February in 15 years,  C@OFC represents Lions Pancake % check,  Rent way up, includes late January income, still best in 15 yrs  Overall for month up $12,000 from last tear and best in 15 yrs. Year-To-Date Income –  Admissions and Gift Shop up over last year  Christmas up $9,500 over 2025  Rent up $5,500 over 2025  Overall up 10% over last year and best in 15 yrs Year-To-Date Expenses –  Salaries/Benefits 2% below benchmark for this point  C@OFC on line with previous years, most bills paid  Overall exactly at benchmark for this period Total Income from all sources Oct/25-Feb/26 $651,196 Total Expenses $653,813 Deficit ($2,617) The Treasurer’s report was Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 3. Site Manager’s report – Bob directed the Board to his attached report in the Board packet. Bob highlighted the Maintenance items for the last month, advertising about San Angelo/Fort Concho in True West, Texas Highways, and the State Travel Guide. III. Regular Agenda 4. Fort Concho/USA 250th Update – Dr. Powers has had lots of media exposure for the special program he has set up. Poster is ready for the next speaker (Thursday March 26 at ASU, Dr. Benjamin Johnson from Loyola University/Chicago). The April 16th event will be back at FC in the Commissary. The FC Speaker Series will start on Wednesday April 1, and it too will have a USA 250th theme. 5. Review of Christmas at Old Fort Concho 2025 and Recommendations for 2026 Event – FC’s Sarah Thieme has lined up some Revolutionary War living history camps. The rate fee(s) discussed last month are grinding through the City’s bureaucracy. Some discussion on an ice-skating rink. Dr. Powers will reach out to ASU on how they did theirs at Christmas. 6. Briefing on Budweiser Clydesdales Visit on April 6-13 – Well under way. Stables provide excellent facilities for the team. 7. Update on Re-scheduling of Chuck Wagon Cook-Off – Tommy Earnest reported the issues that had been raised of continuing the event as planned versus stepping back and re-evaluating how FC needs the event to progress. Postponing to Frontier Day 2027 will be in the Fort’s best interest. 8. Review of Upcoming Events – Info provided in the Board packet. 9. Collections Report – FC Curator Cory Robinson brought a dress uniform coat and dress trousers of a soldier stationed at FC. This was procured through the efforts of Dr. John Langallier, again. Had been in a private collection for 30 years. Also got a helmet used by the 16th Infantry. Quartermaster Sargent George Hollar, served at FC 1880-1885, with total service of 15 yrs in the Army through three (3) enlistments. Cory has records that Hollar married Ann Ranford here in San Angelo in 1884 and died in 1940 at age 82. Coat had some marksmanship medals attached with Hollar’s name on them. 10. 2026 Membership Drive Report – Ongoing at this time, will recede during the San Angelo Gives drive, then back on it at summertime. 11. Update on Fort Concho Social Media – tabled to the April meeting. 12. Approval of Participation in San Angelo Gives and Proposed Project – Dr. Powers made motion for FC to participate in the 2026 San Angelo Gives and seconded by Lisa Marley. Motion carried. With the new LED lighting on Barracks 3-4, it is apparent that the remaining lighting needs to be updated. Bob’s suggestion that this year’s San Angelo Gives project be a lighting upgrade. Our slogan will be “Light Up Fort Concho!”. $25-28K estimated costs. 13. Fort Concho Foundation Report – will meet in April. 14. Update on Barracks 1-2 Visitor Center Project – Fort Concho Foundation funded re-drawing of the plans that are eight years old.. 15. Staff News and Reports – all good at this time. 16. Future Agenda Items & Considerations – Nothing noted at this time. Motion to Adjourn made be Don Barnhart and Seconded by Larry Miller. Motion carried. Meeting Adjourned at 4:30 PM. Next Board meeting Tuesday April 21, 2026. Respectfully Submitted, Tommy Earnest, Secretary /s/ Tommy Earnest Source: https://www.sanangelo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_05192026-110

Download the minutes PDF ↓ Fort Concho Museum Board Minutes April 21, 2026 Officer’s Quarter’s 8 I. OPEN SESSION A. Call to order – Board President Don Barnhart called the Meeting to Order at 3:31 PM. B. Determination of a Quorum – Fort Concho Site Manager Bob Bluthardt confirmed a Quorum was present: Don Barnhart, Monty Stanley, Lisa Marley, Ewell Loudermilk, Tracy Simpson, George Balli, Yukio Kuniyuki, and Tommy Earnest. Absent: Dr. Michael Powers, Lt Col Raymond Kuderka, Penny Roberts, Sarah Cole, Asher Rogers, Larry Miller, and ASU Honors Intern Kaylee Rauch. C. Approval of excused absences – Absences were excused by Board Consensus. D. Introduction of Guests – No guests present E. Presentations – No presentations F. Public Comment – No public comment II. CONSENT AGENDA 1.. Consideration of Approving the March 24, 2026 Minutes – the Minutes were Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 2. Treasurer’s Report – Treasurer Lisa Marley present the following report: This report covers Oct 2025 thru Mar 26, the half-way, 50% mark of the City Fiscal Year. March Monthly Income:  Admissions down; poor weather days and several days of IT issues (Per Bob – 5 days of no internet, 1876 all over again)  Gift Shop up nearly $600  Membership up nearly $6,000  Rent up $1,770  Interest down about $250; varies with the market  Overall; for month up nearly $8,000; best of past 15 years Year-To-Date Income  Admissions and Gift shop both up  C@OFC up $9,100 over 2024  Rent up $7,300 over last year  Donations down from 2025 but well above last years’ average  Special Events (last fall’s Halloween events) down about 10% due to one event night poor weather  Interest about same as 2025  Membership up $6,750 due to slightly earlier mailing and early returns by major donors  Overall; up $66,500 over 2025; best of past 15 years Year-To-Date Expenses  Salaries/Benefits 3% below benchmark for year  Supplies/Services almost 3% below benchmark, but March power bills not posted  C@OFC bills mostly paid; overall total virtually the same as 2024  Other line items below benchmark  Overall; at 48.1% at 50% benchmark; 1% below 2025 Total Revenue from all sources in 2025-2026 $772,516 Total Operating expenses $753,406 Revenue over Expense $19,110 The Treasurer’s report was Approved and Accepted by Board consensus. 3. Site Manager’s Report – Site Manager Bob Bluthardt directed the Board to the attached report in the Board packet. Bob highlighted that a lot of staff activities were going on. Sarah and Eunice attended the state museum meeting in McAllen. Bob stated that letters and postcards were sent out to potential donors for the San Angelo Gives upcoming campaign. The Fort Concho campaign is to replace the old porch lighting to LED to match the new lighting on Barracks 3 & 4. Bob paid homage to Floyd Bias who passed away on March 30. Floyd, a city animal services officer, helped on C@OFC for many years. III. REGULAR AGENDA: PUBLIC HEARING COMMENTS 4. Fort Concho/USA 250th Updates – With Dr. Powers absent, item was tabled to May meeting. The April event had light attendance. FC’s Cory Robinson is the next speaker at ASU with presentation on the gunboat Philadelphia and its connection to FC. 5. Review of Christmas at Old Fort Concho of 2025 and Recommendations for 2026 Event – Staff are recruiting merchants and reenactors. Bringing the chuck wagons back for another teaser. Sarah working on Revolutionary War camp. Don suggested recruiting local musicians to play in the bandstand. 6. Report on Budweiser Clydesdales Visit on April 6-13 – The Clydesdales were awesome and spectacular. 1500-2000 folks on main day at FC. Handlers received FC Challenge Coins. Dalmatians got skunked. Per Tracy, a good turnout when the team went to Goodfellow. 7. Update of Re-Scheduling of Chuck Wagon Cook-Off – Tommy reported to those who missed the last Board meeting on why FC postponed the April 2026 event to April 2027. Tommy made contact with the Abilene cook off folks and will be attending their event May 8-9. 8. Review of Upcoming Events – Frontier Day is next. 1000 expected. 9. Collections Report – Tabled to May meeting 10. 2026 Membership Drive Report – a little less than $35k so far. More push after San Angelo Gives campaign. Per Bob, FC is in good shape financially at this point. 11. Nominations Report – One slot open. Colleen is out. One possible candidate on deck, tbd. 12. Review of FY 2026-2027 Budget Process – FC earns 2/3 of its operating budget. FC has a healthy fund balance at this time with a duration of around 180 days. 13. Update on Fort Concho Social Media – Tabled to May meeting. 14. Fort Concho Foundation Report – had their meeting before the Museum Board meeting. Investments doing well. 15. Update on Barracks 1-2 Visitor Center Project – Check sent to architect to cover initial costs for re-drawing the plans to meet today’s requirements. Slow going as some of the original core team members are no longer available. Original plans were 85% complete. 16. Staff News and Reports – Sarah and Eunice at the state meeting. One open slot in the maintenance dept. 17. Future Agenda Items & Considerations – Polo May 1 & 2. Bandstand tip bucket for C@OFC? Invite area groups. Bob will converse with Carol and Brendalee. Motion to adjourn made by Ewell Loudermilk; seconded by Tracy Simson and approved by all present. Next meeting: Tuesday, May 19, 2026 Side note: There will be a Change-Of-Command Ceremony for Lt Col Kuderka on June 12 at Fort Concho. Respectfully Submitted, Tommy Earnest, Secretary /s/ Tommy Earnest Source: https://www.sanangelo.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_06162026-116

records.summary: A press kit for reporters covering San Angelo
records.text: For journalists — findings, figures and reuse terms | ExposeTexas Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation San Angelo, TX of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Press kit · Updated 25 July 2026 For journalists We are not a newsroom and we are not competing with one. We file records requests and publish documents. If any of it is useful to you, take it — you have blanket permission to reuse everything below with attribution , including our arithmetic. Every figure links to its source. Where a number is ours rather than reported, we say so and show the working. Jump to findings → Primary documents Reuse terms, in plain language Quote us, screenshot our tables, republish our figures, use our computed numbers in your own reporting. Credit ExposeSanAngelo.com or the Move Weight Foundation . You do not need to ask, and there is no embargo on anything published here. We will also, on request and at no cost, file a Texas Public Information Act request on a subject you name and hand you the response unedited — including if you publish it before we do. Email foia@moveweight.com . Six findings, with the working shown Ordered by how checkable they are. The first three are the City's own words or votes. The last three are arithmetic on published figures — our contribution, and we show it so you can verify rather than trust us. 1. The City states no independent impact study was ever conducted “No independent impact study has been conducted.” City of San Angelo, official Data Center Information page This is the City answering its own FAQ about a 1.2 gigawatt facility on land it sold. It is not a characterisation by us or by opponents. sanangelo.gov/803/Data-Center-Information 2. The zoning was locked in five months before any governing ordinance existed Date Action Vote 2025-12-02 Site rezoned Ranch & Estate → Light Manufacturing first reading 2026-01-13 Zone change approved — project now permissible 6–1 2026-05-19 Land use ordinance adopted 6–0 2026-06-02 Sewer / wastewater discharge ordinance adopted 5–1 2026-06-16 Water use ordinance adopted 7–0 The gap between the binding decision and the rules governing it is 126 days. All three ordinances post-date the approval that made them necessary. City of San Angelo (ordinance dates & votes) · Land use ordinance (PDF) · Sewer ordinance (PDF) · Water ordinance (PDF) · SanAngeloLive (rezoning) 3. No executed Chapter 380 agreement has ever been published The City says “to date, there have been no incentives or subsidies offered,” while confirming Chapter 380 terms remain to be negotiated. When draft documents naming Emergent circulated publicly in June 2026, the City's position was that they were examples and that no terms had been decided. Separately, reporting in April 2026 concluded the project will qualify for a large state incentive regardless of local action. The checkable claim As of 25 July 2026 there is no publicly available executed 380 agreement for this project. Every economic figure in circulation is therefore a projection, not a term sheet. We have a records request drafted for the negotiation file. SanAngeloLive — City clarifies no agreement reached · SanAngeloLive — Will qualify for a huge tax incentive · City of San Angelo 4. Our arithmetic 84.9% of the FY26 tax increase falls on existing taxpayers The City published both halves of this but not the ratio. Working: Figure Amount Source Additional property tax to be raised vs. prior year $5,716,170 City, via ConchoValleyHomepage − of which from newly added property $861,795 City, via ConchoValleyHomepage = borne by property already on the roll $4,854,375 subtraction Share carried by existing taxpayers 84.9% 4,854,375 ÷ 5,716,170 Context: the rate rose from 0.75440 to 0.79470 per $100 valuation — a 9.67% increase — adopted 6–1 alongside a $241,308,736 budget. The Finance Director attributed most of it to the coliseum renovation bond. ConchoValleyHomepage — City adopts budget, increased tax rate · Taxes likely to increase for coliseum renovation 5. Our arithmetic The recall threshold for District 3 is 47 signatures — because 155 people voted San Angelo sets a recall petition threshold at 30% of votes cast in the last election for that seat. That produces thresholds two orders of magnitude apart on the same council: Seat Turnout basis Signatures required Outcome Mayor (at-large) — 2,971 Failed — under 1,900 submitted District 2 — Joe Self — 385 Affidavit filed 2026-05-29 District 3 — Harry Thomas 155 votes cast, May 2023 47 Petition filed 2026-07-15 47 signatures can force a recall election in District 3. That is a story about municipal turnout as much as about the data center, and the cost of the election falls on all taxpayers either way. City Clerk Heather Stastny certifies the petitions. SanAngeloLive — Recall petition submitted (47 / 155 figures) · Recall of mayor fails (2,971 figure) · Recalls costly for taxpayers 6. Open question Reported capacity doubled from 600 MW to 1.2 GW with no recorded council action explaining it When Reported capacity Source Dec 2025 up to 600 MW SanAngeloLive Jun 2026 1.2 GW complex SanAngeloLive For scale: the AEP Red Creek substation serving that area is rated around 250 MW, and the entire city of San Angelo is reported to use roughly 10% of it. Final load is set by ERCOT interconnection studies, not by the City — which means the documents that would settle this exist, and are requestable. We are treating this as an open question, not an allegation. SanAngeloLive — 600 MW, substation figures · SanAngeloLive — 1.2 GW · DataCenterDynamics The water numbers, side by side Both sets are on the record and they do not agree. We publish both rather than picking one. Measure City / developer Earlier reporting Initial fill ~2M gal for a 250,000 sq ft building; cap 8.0 gal/sq ft 1.5M gal per building, ~9M across six Ongoing use ~60,000 gal/yr makeup; “near zero” in steady state ~15,000 gal/day Cooling Closed-loop mandatory; evaporative banned — City production ~20 million gallons/day City supply remaining ~41 months; standard conservation in force (outside watering 2×/7 days) Hickory Aquifer allocation 10,000 acre-feet/yr in 2026, rising to 12,000 by 2036 What is missing from both columns No published projection of total campus water demand at full build-out measured against the city's ~41 months of supply. The ordinance caps per square foot, not per campus, and permits a full drain-and-refill every three years. City of San Angelo · Water Resources · Hickory Aquifer · SanAngeloLive What we are and are not claiming We are not claiming corruption. Nothing on this site alleges a crime by any official. Where we describe an allegation we attribute it to whoever made it. We are not anti-data-center. The City adopted mandatory closed-loop cooling and banned evaporative cooling, 7–0. That is the strongest water protection available to a city in this position and we say so on our own water page. Our objection is to sequence and disclosure — a binding vote 126 days before the rules, and an unpublished 380 agreement underneath every economic projection. We correct errors on the page, not quietly. Any official named on this site may send a response of reasonable length and we will publish it in full, unedited. No developer, candidate, PAC, or party money. We do not scrape, mirror, or republish other newsrooms' articles — only link to them. If you would prefer we not link to a particular piece, tell us and we will remove it.

records.summary: File an open records request against the City of San Angelo, Tom Green County, SAISD or the appraisal district. The Move Weight Foundation files as the requester so your name never appears. Free, with a correctly-cited TPIA PDF generated for you.
records.text: File a Texas Public Information Act request — free, anonymous | ExposeTexas Skip to content Public request queue & statutory clock Every request filed through this site. Texas gives each body 10 business days from receipt to produce records, ask the Attorney General for permission to withhold, or state that it needs more time (Gov't Code §552.301). The clock below is computed from the filing date, skipping weekends. We publish it whether it flatters the City or not. — Requests filed — Awaiting response — Past statutory deadline — Records produced Loading the queue… Business-day arithmetic excludes Saturdays and Sundays. It does not attempt to exclude Texas state holidays or the City's own skeleton-crew days, so a request shown as one or two days late may not in fact be late. We would rather understate that than overstate it — treat the count as indicative and check the specific request before reporting it as a violation. Who holds what Verified contacts for the records custodians covering San Angelo and Tom Green County. If you would rather file directly yourself, everything you need is here — we would genuinely rather you did that than not file at all. Body Custodian & contact Accepted method City of San Angelo Most city records Heather Stastny, City Clerk / Records Management Officer heather.stastny@sanangelo.gov Barbara Stallworth, Deputy City Clerk barbara.stallworth@sanangelo.gov 72 W. College Ave, 2nd floor, San Angelo TX 76903 · 325-657-4405 Mon–Fri 8–12, 1–5 Portal preferred Public Records Center San Angelo Police Dept. Incident & accident reports Records Division 401 E Beauregard Ave (in person) Attn: Records Division, PO Box 5020, San Angelo TX 76902 (mail) Mon–Fri 8:00–4:30 · cash, check, or money order Mail or in person only Explicitly does not accept email, fax, or phone Tom Green County Clerk 112 W. Beauregard Ave, 2nd floor, San Angelo TX 76903 · 325-659-6556 Mail / in person Tom Green County District Clerk 112 W. Beauregard Ave, San Angelo TX 76903 · 325-659-6579 Mail / in person San Angelo ISD Communications Dept., 1621 University Ave, San Angelo TX 76904 NextRequest portal SAISD requests Tom Green County Appraisal District Tyler Johnson, Chief Appraiser · 2302 Pulliam St, San Angelo TX 76905 · 325-658-5575 Mail / in person Contacts verified July 2026 against each body's own published pages. Government contacts change — if you find one of these stale, tell us . Know your rights under the Act What is public. Almost everything. Emails, text messages about city business, contracts, invoices, calendars, memos, studies, bid documents, personnel policies, body camera policies, budget worksheets. The presumption in Texas law is disclosure. What can be withheld. Narrow categories — certain law enforcement records, attorney-client communications, some personnel matters, competitive bidding information before award. Crucially, a body that wants to withhold must normally ask the Attorney General for permission within 10 business days . Silence is not a valid denial. What you never have to do. Explain why you want it. State your purpose. Prove you are a resident. A governmental body may not require a reason as a condition of release. What costs money. Copies, not access. If a body estimates over $40 in charges it must give you a written itemized estimate first. Authoritative sources: Texas AG — How to Request Public Information · Overview of the Public Information Act · Public Information Act Handbook 2024 (PDF) This is a plain-language summary of a statute, not legal advice. The Move Weight Foundation is not a law firm. For a dispute over a denial, the Texas Attorney General's Open Government Hotline is 1-877-673-6839. 501(c)(3) · Tax-deductible Every request has a price tag $0.10 a page adds up fast when the answer is a 400-page agenda packet. Donations pay copy fees, certified copies, postage, and the occasional Attorney General filing — nothing else. Fund a records request Send by Zelle to team@moveweight.com — it reaches the Move Weight Foundation's nonprofit bank account. A dedicated San Angelo GoFundMe is being set up; we are deliberately not routing San Angelo donations to the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma campaign. · IRS Form 990
